claim:
For the equal-mass Majumdar–Papapetrou dihole on the symmetry plane \(z=0\), in units where the half-separation is \(1\), let \(M_*=\sqrt{27/8}\), \(\rho_*=\sqrt{5}\), \(\delta=M-M_*>0\), \(\rho_0=\rho_*+\sqrt{\delta}X\), \(\Phi(X)=aX-bX^3\), \(a=128\sqrt{30}/703125\), \(b=8\sqrt{5}/140625\), and \(c=\sqrt{a/(3b)}=\sqrt{16\sqrt{6}/15}\). For each fixed \(X>c\) or \(X<-2c\), the equatorial scattering deflection angle obeys
\[
\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}\delta^{1/4}\bigl[\hat\alpha(\rho_0;M)+\pi\bigr]
=\frac{8}{125}\int_X^\infty\frac{dY}{\sqrt{\Phi(X)-\Phi(Y)}}.
\]

correctness.rationale: At the critical point V_rho=V_rhorho=0, V_rhoM=a>0 and V_rhorhorho=-6b<0. The delta^(3/2) cubic normal form follows from Taylor expansion under rho-rho_*=sqrt(delta)X. Substitution in the exact deflection integral gives delta^(-1/4) and coefficient 2 sqrt(V_*)/rho_*=8/125. The two open branch domains ensure a positive denominator; a separate tail estimate controls the full integral.

value.rationale: The two endpoint regimes have different singular laws, so their separate approximations are nonuniform near the photon-ring merger. The explicit scaled integral identifies the intermediate delta^(-1/4) regime, gives the exact normalization and admissible branches, and matches the logarithmic endpoint singularities and the critical |rho_0-rho_*|^(-1/2) behavior.
